description:
Checks resume text for machine-readable sections, recognized skills, contact channels, a headline,
and experience date ranges using FoundRole's deterministic parser.

resume_text checks plain text supplied in the conversation. resume_id selects an upload or editable version
owned by the authenticated user, when its FoundRole ID is known. An explicit check accepts one of these
inputs. With neither input the tool reads the primary upload. A version check reads its current plain-text rendering.
It returns a readability band (strong, good, partial) and the single biggest loss. Depending on the
account it also returns additional findings and the parsed facts (headline, years of experience,
sections, contact channels, recognized skill count). Each finding includes a suggested fix.
A completed check can offer an optional step to take the resume into Resume Studio. A checked saved upload can include parserReportUrl for the same upload in Resume Studio. This is FoundRole's text-readability assessment,
not a test against a named ATS, a hiring prediction, or a file-layout check. Pasted text does not
preserve the original PDF or DOCX layout.

The tool does not upload a file, create a saved resume or report, change the user's profile, submit an
application, or fetch URLs found in the text. It may return a FoundRole website link; opening that link
and uploading or editing a resume are separate user actions. Operational request records and diagnostics
may retain tool inputs; this tool does not promise that submitted text is never stored.

resume_id.description: FoundRole ID of the owned upload or editable version to check instead of pasted text.

resume_text.description: Plain text of the resume to check, when it is available in the conversation. Omit to check the resume uploaded to the user's FoundRole account. Minimum 200 characters.

name: resume_check
title: Check how hiring software reads a resume
